hints: Start at the very beginning with the macrophage. What must happen to the pathogen before T-helper cells can get involved at all?
Remember the order of clonal expansion: T-helper cells must first switch on B-cells, then B-cells divide by mitosis to make plasma cells, and only plasma cells can release antibodies.
walkthrough:
**Start with antigen presentation**

Think like the immune system. First a macrophage engulfs and digests the pathogen, then displays its antigens. That is step Q, so Q must be first.

Q comes before any lymphocyte activation can happen.

**T-helper cells act as coordinators**

Once Q has happened, the T-helper cell recognises that presented antigen and becomes activated. It then releases cytokines to activate other lymphocytes, including B-lymphocytes. That is step S, so S is second.

**Clonal expansion then antibody production**

After being activated by T-helpers, the specific B-lymphocytes divide rapidly by mitosis to make a large clone. That is step P, so P is third. Some of those cloned cells then differentiate into plasma cells which secrete antibodies, which is step R, so R is fourth and last.

Correct order: Q -> S -> P -> R, so third is P.

options.A: P is correct because B-lymphocyte mitosis (clonal expansion) happens after T-helper activation but before plasma cells exist to secrete antibodies, making it third.
options.B: Q is false for third because interaction of T-helpers with antigen-presenting macrophages is the initiating event, so it is first.
options.C: R is false for third because antibody secretion by plasma cells is the final outcome after cloning and differentiation, so it is fourth.
options.D: S is false for third because T-helper cells activate other lymphocytes soon after antigen presentation, so it is second.
